reasons: Both find the off-by-one with a correct worked example, give a fix that returns exactly n items across the range, and keep clear of any send-timing advice. B separates the three failure modes, states the contract in a docstring, explains why only n <= 0 needs a guard, and supplies runnable asserts covering n=0, n == len, n > len and the empty list, which makes it the more actionable review. A is close and adds a useful boundary table plus the items[-n:] n=0 trap, but its tests stay a prose checklist and it omits the non-sliceable-input case B covers with deque(maxlen=n).
